speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) what the sizes of the largest available public rental flats in each decade since 1965 are; (b) why the sizes have changed, and (c) whether the size of new public rental flats built since 2006 are suited for large families.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) whether there is a limit to the number of occupants for HDB's rental flats; and (b) whether the Ministry has plans to introduce basic occupancy standards for these rental flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I am taking Question Nos 32 and 33 together, with your permission, Sir.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The rental rates for these 1- and 2-room public rental flats are heavily subsidised so that they remain accessible to the lower-income households.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And we take a similar approach for flats which are sold or rented in the open market because, in the same manner, there is no limit on the number of related persons who can stay together as a family in these units.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will continue to review how best to meet the needs of public rental households, including larger families, as part of the Government's broader effort to support vulnerable families.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The Minister mentioned that larger family units can rent two separate rental flats.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: How many of these families have applied for them, and how many have been approved so far?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This also goes back to the reason why we have to better understand the needs of the families we are talking about.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: When HDB closed the 3-room register in 1982, the experience was that many of these families, in fact, preferred to buy, rather than to rent, the 3-room flats because it made more financial sense for them.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They could pay using their Central Provident Fund and, at the end of the day, they would have a flat of their own.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, if you were to talk larger families who want to apply for two separate units, they would have to pay a larger rental amount.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Some of them may prefer not to do so.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If it is a first-timer family, they may very well prefer to build up their savings first in order to buy a flat later.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, I think there are multiple needs here.
